reviewed_by: Codex review of project goal-skill shared-rule persistence
reason: Project-owned skills intentionally share instructions through the project's .agents/rules tree, but goal skill snapshots rejected every reference outside the individual skill directory. The resolver now derives a source-aware boundary from the discovered catalog entry: project skills may snapshot exact, digested resources within the same .agents tree, while installed skills remain confined to their own directory. Focused unit tests cover successful shared-rule reads, traversal rejection, and symlink rejection; API coverage proves durable goal mutation; provider chat tests cover snapshot use; the real-Core browser journey proves save and reload from the operator entry point on desktop and emulated Chromium/WebKit mobile profiles.
exclusions: No frontend unit test is selected because UI request construction and local interaction are unchanged; the existing production real-Core Playwright journey exercises the exact Save skills control, API mutation, visible count, reload, retained source-loss state, and subsequent provider use. No native tests because Rust and the desktop shell are unchanged. Provider transport, unrelated chat lifecycle, harness-native goals, MCP, workspace mutation, and full suites are excluded. No CSS audit is selected because no styles or rendered copy changed.
